title: Coding a Binary-Choice Machine
statement: For every finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ over the binary alphabet, there is a machine $M$ with a finite number of work tapes, states indexed by an initial segment of the natural numbers, and binary-choice transitions such that, for every binary input $x$ and every choice word $w$, the run of $M$ halts if and only if the run of $N$ halts, and both runs produce exactly the same output.
hypotheses_covered: N is a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine over Bool
